sourceReviews.supportingSummary: Independently read the actual AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS (Transact-SQL) receipt, including Applies to, Prerequisites, and both authentication variants of the end-to-end example. The prerequisite code enables sp_configure 'external rest endpoint enabled', 1 and reconfigures. The accompanying note explicitly says that option is enabled by default on Azure SQL Database and Fabric SQL database. The API-key example enables REST invocation without the managed-identity option; the managed-identity example separately enables host credentials and REST invocation. These establish the server control and platform/authentication distinctions in the question. The prerequisite prose abbreviates the endpoint procedure's name, but the tested server option is stated consistently in the actual commands. The unrelated conflicting embedding return-type paragraph does not determine a configuration-option answer.

Independently read CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL (Transact-SQL), especially Managed identity, remote API-key examples, and the complete Example with ONNX Runtime running locally section. The managed-identity section associates 'allow server scoped db credentials' with using the SQL Server 2025 Arc/VM host's managed identity as a database credential. The local ONNX workflow applies to SQL Server 2025 on Windows, requires Machine Learning Services, enables PREVIEW_FEATURES, then enables 'external AI runtimes enabled', and separately configures runtime/model files and permissions. These are real positive uses for the two distractor settings, not alternative names for remote REST enablement. The local path is explicitly Preview; the candidate's remote HTTPS/API-key scope neither requires nor denies that separate capability.

choiceReviews.rationale: Enable external rest endpoint enabled is the exact server option in the embedding function's prerequisite and remote API-key example. The stem states that remote REST invocation has not been enabled on this SQL Server 2025 instance while model/caller configuration is ready, so this is the missing control. Literal confirming context: an authorized server configurator prepares this same Windows SQL Server instance for its configured remote HTTPS embedding endpoint using the documented sp_configure option and reconfiguration sequence. This identifies the setting; it does not assert that model EXECUTE permission by itself authorizes server administration or that merely granting a permission changes configuration.

Enabling external AI runtimes enabled belongs to the local AI Runtime Host/ONNX workflow, not the stipulated remote HTTPS invocation route. Literal positive countercontext: a SQL Server 2025 Windows deployment intentionally prepares the documented Preview local ONNX runtime, with Machine Learning Services installed and PREVIEW_FEATURES enabled; enabling this exact server option is then the local-runtime configuration step described in Step 2. Runtime/model libraries, directory access and other documented setup remain separate prerequisites, so the option alone is not claimed to complete the installation. This real Preview use is excluded by the remote endpoint scenario.

Enable allow server scoped db credentials addresses use of the Arc/VM host's managed identity as a database-level credential, not the missing external REST invocation switch. The current scenario already uses a configured API-key credential. Literal positive countercontext: SQL Server 2025 on an appropriately configured Arc/VM host must use that host's managed identity as its database credential, and an authorized administrator enables this exact option as instructed by the product reference's Managed identity section. REST invocation is still a separate setting, as the embedding reference's managed-identity example also shows. I do not claim that either setting performs a grant or that enabling host credentials alone enables HTTP calls.

Relying on Azure SQL Database's enabled-by-default setting cannot enable the explicitly not-enabled Windows SQL Server instance that will make these calls. Literal positive countercontext preserving the action and leaving this instance unchanged: the workload's outbound calls execute in the team's already configured Azure SQL Database environment instead of the Windows instance. The documented Azure SQL Database default can then be relied on for those Azure calls, while the unused Windows instance need not be changed. That does not make the Windows instance enabled. The reference's default note names Azure SQL Database and Fabric SQL database; it does not transfer either cloud default to the stipulated SQL Server deployment.
